# Load the libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
# library(paletteer)

# This is the data with the annotated and predicted values (with annotation, visible lipid sac, no visible lipid sac). So make sure to curate first and that an object_id is only considered once. This file also contains a table of the annotated data, and the original list of UVP6 metadata with morphological descriptors (including the images excluded because outside the size range).
load("data/uvp6_lipids_20250410.RData")

theme_set(theme_bw())
`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)


calc_r2 <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.numeric(x) && is.numeric(y) && length(na.omit(x)) > 1 && length(na.omit(y)) > 1) {
    df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
    model <- lm(y ~ x, data = df, na.action = na.omit)
    return(round(summary(model)$r.squared, 3))
  } else {
    return(NA) # Return NA if column is not numeric or has insufficient data
  }
}
```

# Curate the lipid segmentation data
```{r}
uvp6 <- uvp6_all %>% 
  # remove the predictions for images with manually annotated data
  filter(type != "predicted") %>% 
  
  # # include the metadata for images segmented but excluded?
  # bind_rows(uvp6_meta %>% 
  #             filter(object_id %notin% uvp6_all$object_id)) %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>% 
  mutate(Year = year(date),
         Month = month(date),
         DOY = yday(date)) %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 8, "August", "")) %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 9, "September", Month2)) %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 10, "October", Month2)) %>% 
  select(-Month) %>% rename(Month = Month2) %>% 
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = c("August","September","October")))

# Make sure that an image is not considered twice. This has to match number of rows 
length(unique(uvp6$object_id)) == nrow(uvp6)

rm(uvp6_all, uvp6_volumes)
```

# Derive volume, DW, carbon
Note that the Vogedes equations to get lipid carbon weight (based on 3 Calanus species) results in slightly larger values compared to the Tarling equations which were set for C. finmarchicus.
```{r}
# TODO calculate the biovolume, dry weight, prosome and lipid mass in carbon, and lipid fullness in carbon
uvpRes <- 0.084
# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmid et al. 2018 based on 36-carbon chain lengths in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- (36*12) / (36*12 + 2*36 + 2*16)
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)


uvp6 <- uvp6 %>% 
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
    # Convert pixel area to mm2
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
  
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome / (pi * prosomeMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
  mutate(minor_lipid_derived = (lipid / (pi * lipidMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
  
  
  # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * (prosomeMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation.. according to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipidMajor * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
  # # Calculate lipid sac volume based spheroid (results in slightly larger volume)
  # mutate(lipid_volume_mm3_sph = 
  #          4/3 * pi * (lipidMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_lipid_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2))

  
  # Calculate lipid fullness based on volume
  mutate(lipidfullness_volume  = (lipid_volume_mm3/prosome_biovolume_mm3 * 100)) %>% 
  
  # (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
  
  # TODO CLARIFY Calculate prosome carbon weight (** NOTE: many options ***)

  # Option 1: Use prosome length to volume (mm3) and calculate dry weight and mg C (Jonasdottir et al. 2019 for C. finmarchicus)
  mutate(prosome_volume_Jonasdottir = 
           0.0292 * (prosomeMajor * uvpRes)^3.6699,
         prosome_dryweight_Jonasdottir = 
           0.0106 * (prosomeMajor * uvpRes)^3.64,
         prosome_mgC_Jonasdottir = 
           0.623 * prosome_dryweight_Jonasdottir - 0.0143) %>% 
  
    # Option 2: Direct biovolume --> carbon mass based on conversion factors in McConville et al. 2016 assuming 1 mm3 = 1 mg wet weight
  mutate(prosome_mgC_McConville = 
           prosome_biovolume_mm3 * vol2massC) %>% 
  
  
  # Option 3: Lucie's coefficient for conversion is 0.9 (20% wet weight, 45% carbon in dry weight). Not that this is calculated from area and not volume
  mutate(structural_carbon = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 0.2 * 0.45) %>%  # Ikeda et al., 1989
  mutate(prosome_mgC_Bourreau = structural_carbon + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
# ** Note that wax ester mass is used here but Lucie's code seems to use lipid area/volume and multiplied with 0.79 Tarling et al. (2022) coefficient
  
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon
  mutate(
    LF_carbon_Jonasdottir = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_Jonasdottir * 100,
    LF_carbon_McConville = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_McConville * 100,
    LF_carbon_Bourreau = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_Bourreau * 100)


# For now the bases of values are the following
uvp6 <- uvp6 %>% 
  select(object_id:prosomeMajor, type:time, Depth_5m:prosome_area_mm2,
         prosome_biovolume_mm3,
         waxester_mass_mg,
         waxester_mass_mgC,
         structural_carbon,
         prosome_mgC_Bourreau,
         lipidfullness_volume,
         LF_carbon_Bourreau,
         annotation:PerimMajor )
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Prosome ellipsoid minor axis versus derived
ggplot(uvp6, aes(x = prosomeMinor * uvpRes, y = minor_derived * uvpRes)) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point() +
  annotate("text", x = max(uvp6$prosomeMinor * uvpRes, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(uvp6$minor_derived * uvpRes, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(uvp6$prosomeMinor, 
                                             uvp6$minor_derived)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
```

## LF prediction accuracy
Compare the annotated and predicted values for lipid fullness calculated three ways.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
# NOTE: need to uncomment the exclusion of predicted images when loading the data

uvp6.sub <- uvp6 %>% 
  filter(type %in% c("annotated","predicted")) %>% 
  group_by(object_id) %>% 
  filter(n()>=2) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(object_id, type, 
         LFarea = lipidfullness,
         LFvolume = lipidfullness_volume,
         LFcarbon = LF_carbon_Bourreau) %>% 
  mutate(LFarea = LFarea * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = type,
              values_from = c(LFarea, LFvolume, LFcarbon))

cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(uvp6.sub, aes(x = LFarea_annotated, y = LFarea_predicted)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", x = max(uvp6.sub$LFarea_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(uvp6.sub$LFarea_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(uvp6.sub$LFarea_annotated, 
                                             uvp6.sub$LFarea_predicted)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("LF Area annotated") + ylab("LF Area predicted"),
  
  ggplot(uvp6.sub, aes(x = LFvolume_annotated, y = LFvolume_predicted)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", x = max(uvp6.sub$LFvolume_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(uvp6.sub$LFvolume_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(uvp6.sub$LFvolume_annotated, 
                                             uvp6.sub$LFvolume_predicted)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("LF Volume annotated") + ylab("LF Volume predicted"),
  
  ggplot(uvp6.sub, aes(x = LFcarbon_annotated, y = LFcarbon_predicted)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", x = max(uvp6.sub$LFcarbon_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(uvp6.sub$LFcarbon_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(uvp6.sub$LFcarbon_annotated, 
                                             uvp6.sub$LFcarbon_predicted)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("LF Carbon annotated") + ylab("LF Carbon predicted"),
  
  labels = "auto", nrow = 1
)

ggsave("figures/UVP6_LF_accuracy.png",
       height = 4, width = 8, units = "in")
```


# Random forest model of structural carbon and lipid carbon prediction
When models are developed with n = 6608 images, struct_carbon has 93.23% var explained and wax ester carbon has 89.97% var explained.

When models are developed with the n = 1806 images with annotations, struct_carbon has 92.61% var explained (RMSR = 0.167)and wax ester carbon has 87.76% var explained (RMSR = 0.253). So it is comparable.

The test for the with no annotation predictions resulted in accuracy of...

```{r}
library(randomForest)
library(randomForestExplainer)

# subset data to simply be StructCarbon, WaxEster, + predictors
uvp6_for_rf <- uvp6 %>% 
  filter(type != "predicted") %>%
  filter(type == "annotated") %>% # do the model on the annotated data only
  filter(!is.na(structural_carbon)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(waxester_mass_mgC)) %>% 
  select(structural_carbon, waxester_mass_mgC,
         Major:PerimMajor) 


# Random forest regression on structural carbon mass
set.seed(888)
model.prosome <- randomForest(structural_carbon ~ .,
                      data = uvp6_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-c(waxester_mass_mgC)), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)
model.prosome 
plot(model.prosome)

# Try random forest regression on lipid (wax ester) mass
set.seed(888)
model.lipid <- randomForest(waxester_mass_mgC ~ .,
                      data = uvp6_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-c(structural_carbon)), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)
model.lipid 
plot(model.lipid)
```

## Evaluate RF models
### ordination of the RF results
```{r, eval=FALSE}
dist.mat <- dist(1 - model.lipid$proximity)
mds.stuff <- cmdscale(dist.mat, eig = TRUE, x.ret = TRUE)
mds.var.per <- round(mds.stuff$eig/sum(mds.stuff$eig)*100,1)

mds.values <- mds.stuff$points
mds.data <- data.frame(Sample = rownames(mds.values),
                       X = mds.values[,1],
                       Y = mds.values[,2],
                       Lipid = uvp6_for_rf$waxester_mass_mgC)

ggplot(data = mds.data, 
       aes(x = X, y = Y, label = Sample)) +
  geom_text(aes(color = Lipid)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  xlab(paste("MDS1 - ", mds.var.per[1], "%")) +
  
  ylab(paste("MDS2 - ", mds.var.per[2], "%")) +
  ggtitle("RF Lipid mass")


dist.mat <- dist(1 - model.prosome$proximity)
mds.stuff <- cmdscale(dist.mat, eig = TRUE, x.ret = TRUE)
mds.var.per <- round(mds.stuff$eig/sum(mds.stuff$eig)*100,1)

mds.values <- mds.stuff$points
mds.data <- data.frame(Sample = rownames(mds.values),
                       X = mds.values[,1],
                       Y = mds.values[,2],
                       Prosome = uvp6_for_rf$structural_carbon)

ggplot(data = mds.data, 
       aes(x = X, y = Y, label = Sample)) +
  geom_text(aes(color = Prosome)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  xlab(paste("MDS1 - ", mds.var.per[1], "%")) +
  
  ylab(paste("MDS2 - ", mds.var.per[2], "%")) +
  ggtitle("RF Prosome mass")


```

### importance of parameters
Generally, the RF models mainly use area, and dimensions (major, feret, minor, perim) to model both prosome and lipid mass. Is this just a fancy allometric scaling model? The lipid mass predictor does value Fractal more which indicates that there is something more to this.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
cowplot::plot_grid(
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.prosome, size_measure = "no_of_nodes"),
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.prosome, x_measure = "mse_increase", y_measure = "node_purity_increase", size_measure = "p_value", no_of_labels = 5),
  labels = "auto")

ggsave("figures/UVP6_rf_structural_importance.png",
       height = 4, width = 9, units = "in")


cowplot::plot_grid(
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.lipid, size_measure = "no_of_nodes"),
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.lipid, x_measure = "mse_increase", y_measure = "node_purity_increase", size_measure = "p_value", no_of_labels = 5),
  labels = "auto")

ggsave("figures/UVP6_rf_waxester_importance.png",
       height = 4, width = 9, units = "in")
```


### Predicted vs annoated
```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Apply the model to the new images with predicted segmentations
uvp6_for_rf_prediction <- uvp6 %>% 
  filter(type != "predicted") %>%
  filter(type != "annotated") %>% # do the model on the annotated data only
  filter(!is.na(structural_carbon)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(waxester_mass_mgC)) %>% 
  select(type, 
         structural_carbon_seg = structural_carbon, 
         waxester_mass_mgC_seg = waxester_mass_mgC,
         Major:PerimMajor)

rf_pred_prosome <- predict(model.prosome,
                           uvp6_for_rf_prediction %>% 
                             select(-c(type, structural_carbon_seg,
                                       waxester_mass_mgC_seg)))


rf_pred_lipid <- predict(model.lipid,
                           uvp6_for_rf_prediction %>% 
                             select(-c(type, structural_carbon_seg,
                                       waxester_mass_mgC_seg)))

# Create a dataframe of the segmentation_predicted and rf_predicted
results_rf_seg <- uvp6_for_rf_prediction %>% 
  select(type, structural_carbon_seg, waxester_mass_mgC_seg) 
results_rf_seg$structural_carbon_rf <- rf_pred_prosome
results_rf_seg$waxester_mass_mgC_rf <- rf_pred_lipid


# Plot comparison
cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(results_rf_seg, aes(x = structural_carbon_seg, 
                             y = structural_carbon_rf)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", 
             x = max(results_rf_seg$structural_carbon_seg, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(results_rf_seg$structural_carbon_rf, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(results_rf_seg$structural_carbon_seg,             results_rf_seg$structural_carbon_rf)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("Structural carbon - segmentation") + 
    ylab("Structural carbon - random forest"),
  
   ggplot(results_rf_seg, aes(x = waxester_mass_mgC_seg, 
                              y = waxester_mass_mgC_rf)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", 
             x = max(results_rf_seg$waxester_mass_mgC_seg, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(results_rf_seg$waxester_mass_mgC_rf, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(results_rf_seg$waxester_mass_mgC_seg,
                                             results_rf_seg$waxester_mass_mgC_rf)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("Wax ester - segmentation") + 
    ylab("Wax ester - random forest"),
  
  labels = "auto"
```

## Basic allometric scaling equations, get R2 and compare performance with RF and CNN models
```{r, eval=FALSE}
# OLS regression model function
getRegressionModel <- function(df, X, Y, base = "10") {
  trait.sub <- df %>% 
    filter(!is.na(get(X)) & !is.na(get(Y))) %>% 
    relocate(X, Y)
  
  if (nrow(trait.sub) > 3) {
    # Calculate OLS
    if(base == "10") {
      reg <- lm(log10(get(Y)) ~ log10(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
    } else if (base == "e") {
      reg <- lm(log(get(Y)) ~ log(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
    } else if (base == "none") {
      reg <- lm(get(Y) ~ get(X), data = trait.sub)
    } else {
      stop("Error: Please select either base 10, e, or none.")
    }
    
    reg.results <- data.frame(X = X,  Y = Y, 
                              a = reg$coefficients[1],
                              b = reg$coefficients[2],
                              n = nrow(trait.sub),
                              R2 = summary(reg)$adj.r.squared,
                              RSE = summary(reg)$sigma,
                              pval = getpval(summary(reg)$fstatistic), 
                              model = "OLS", base = as.character(base),
                              minX = min(trait.sub[,1]), maxX = max(trait.sub[,1]))
  } else {
    reg.results <- data.frame(X = X,  Y = Y, 
                              a = NA, b = NA, n = nrow(trait.sub),
                              R2 = NA, RSE = NA, pval = NA, 
                              model = "OLS", base = as.character(base),
                              minX = NA, maxX = NA)
  }
  
  return(reg.results %>% 
           remove_rownames())
}

getpval <- function(x){ 
  p <- pf(x[1],x[2],x[3],lower.tail = F) 
  attributes(p) <- NULL
  return(p)
}


allom_sub <- uvp6_for_rf %>% 
  select(structural_carbon, waxester_mass_mgC, Area, Major, Perim, Feret)

# prepare data frame of models to test
reg.models <- data.frame( modelNum = c(1:9),
                          X = c("structural_carbon", 
                                "Area", "Major", 
                                "Perim", "Feret",
                                "Area", "Major", 
                                "Perim", "Feret"),
                          Y = c("waxester_mass_mgC", 
                                "waxester_mass_mgC", "waxester_mass_mgC", 
                                "waxester_mass_mgC", "waxester_mass_mgC",
                                "structural_carbon", "structural_carbon",
                                "structural_carbon", "structural_carbon") ) %>% 
  mutate(model = "OLS", 
         base = "none")

# survey linear regression models
reg.results <- data.frame()
for (i in c(1:nrow(reg.models))){
  reg.results <- bind_rows(reg.results, 
                           getRegressionModel(allom_sub, 
                                              reg.models$X[i], reg.models$Y[i],
                                              base = reg.models$base[i]))
}
```

## Apply random forest models to all other calanoida/copepoda images within the size range of the annotated images

There are 25,878 total zooplankton images, 6,625 images are copepods with segmentations (26%). There are 14,029 are copepods without segmentations (54%) which include 91,69 are copepods without segmentations but within the size range of the annotated data (35%). Thus, 20% of images are smaller copepods based on major axis length and are excluded from any lipid mass prediction. There were no copepods larger than what was manually segmented. Majority of copepods with no segmentations and within the size range were classified generally as "Copepoda" (95%) while there were 241 images of Calanus (the ones excluded by the poor segmentations) and 115 for Metridia (both totalling 4%). Depending on how confident we are with extrapolating the biomass estimation using a random forest model, we can have carbon values for 60% of all the images, which likely translates to a larger percentage if based on biomass.
```{r}
# The uvp6 data from ecotaxa
load("data/uvp6_deam_living_20250320.RData")

# Merge the 2021 an 2023 data 
uvp6_ecotaxa <- bind_rows(uvp6_de, uvp6_am) 
rm(uvp6_de, uvp6_am)


# Of the copepods with no segmentations, how many are within the size range of the annotated data
cope_for_rf <- uvp6_ecotaxa %>%
  filter(object_id %notin% uvp6$object_id) %>% 
  filter(taxagroup == "Copepoda") %>% 
  filter(object_major >= filter(uvp6_annot_table, column == "Major")$min &
           object_major <= filter(uvp6_annot_table, column == "Major")$max) %>% 
  # exclude Oncaeidae (62) and Paraeuchata (11)?
  filter(taxaname %notin% c("Oncaeidae","Paraeuchaeta")) %>% 
  # select and rename columns
  select(object_id,
         Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, 
         Perim = object_perim.,
         Feret = object_feret, Area = object_.area, 
         Elongation = object_elongation,
         VerSym = object_symetriev, VerSym2 = object_symetrievc, 
         Circ = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
         MeanGrey = object_mean, MedGrey = object_median,
         HistGrey75 = object_histcum3, SdevGrey = object_stddev, 
         SkewGrey = object_skew, Fractal = object_fractal, 
         PerimFeret = object_perimferet, 
         PerimMajor = object_perimmajor)
  
cope_rf_meta <- uvp6_ecotaxa %>% 
  filter(object_id %in% cope_for_rf$object_id) %>% 
    select(object_id, taxagroup, taxaname,
         lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, 
         depth = object_depth_min,
         date = object_date, time = object_time,
         sample_id, sample_cruise) %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>% 
  mutate(Year = year(date),
         Month = month(date),
         DOY = yday(date)) %>% 
  mutate(Year = as.factor(Year))

# cope_for_rf %>% 
#   group_by(taxaname) %>% 
#   count()

# Estimate carbon content 
cope_rf <- cope_for_rf
cope_rf$structural_carbon <- predict(model.prosome,
                                            cope_for_rf %>% 
                                              select(-c(object_id)))

cope_rf$waxester_carbon <- predict(model.lipid,
                                            cope_for_rf %>% 
                                              select(-c(object_id)))
cope_rf <- cope_rf %>% 
  mutate(total_carbon = structural_carbon + waxester_carbon) %>% 
  mutate(lf_carbon = waxester_carbon / total_carbon * 100)


cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(cope_rf, aes(x = Major, y = structural_carbon)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(),
  
  ggplot(cope_rf, aes(x = Major, y = waxester_carbon)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(),
  labels = "auto"
)

ggsave("figures/UVP6_randomforest_for_copepoda_without_seg.png",
       height = 4, width = 6, units = "in")

# Export random forest predicted carbon values
save(cope_rf, cope_rf_meta, model.prosome, model.lipid,
     file = "data/uvp6_randomforest_results_20240411.RData")
```

```{r}
  select(-c(taxagroup, taxaname)) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(as.character(Year))) %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 8, "August", "")) %>%

  select(-Month) %>% rename(Month = Month2) %>% 
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = c("August","September","October"))) 

cope_carbon_meta <- cope_rf_meta %>% 
  bind_rows(uvp6 %>% 
              select(colnames(cope_rf_meta))) %>% 
  # Add the volume measurements for the random forest data

  left_join(uvp6_ecopart,
            by = join_by(sample_id, Depth_5m))
```

```{r}
# Establish the depth bins

  mutate(depthBin = floor(Depth_5m/binsize)*binsize) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, depthBin) %>% 
  summarise(volume_m3 = sum(Sampled_volume_m3),
            nbins = n(), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(binsize = binsize) %>% 
  mutate(depthRange = paste0(depthBin,"m - ",depthBin+binsize,"m"))
uvp6_ecopartBin <- uvp6_ecopartBin %>% 
  mutate(depthRange = factor(depthRange,
                             levels = unique(uvp6_ecopartBin$depthRange)))

# Calculate abundance, total carbon biomass per depth bin (average across 130 samples)
cope_bin <- cope_carbon %>% 
  filter(!is.na(structural_carbon)) %>% 
  left_join(cope_carbon_meta, by = "object_id") %>% 
  # Add the total volume for the depth bin
  mutate(depthBin = floor(Depth_5m/binsize)*binsize) %>% 
  select(-c(Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_L, Sampled_volume_m3)) %>% 
  left_join(uvp6_ecopartBin,
            by = join_by(sample_id, depthBin)) %>% 
  # Calculate the abundance and carbon density per depth bin (/m3)
  # TODO can bin by data source here too
  group_by(depthBin, depthRange,
           lon, lat, Year, Month, DOY, volume_m3) %>% 
  summarise(abundance = n(), #
            structural_carbon = sum(structural_carbon),
            waxester_carbon = sum(waxester_carbon),
            total_carbon = sum(total_carbon),
            lf_carbon_mean = mean(lf_carbon),
            lf_carbon_sd = sd(lf_carbon),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(abundance_m3 = abundance / volume_m3,
         structural_carbon_m3 = structural_carbon / volume_m3,
         waxester_carbon_m3 = waxester_carbon / volume_m3,
```

```{r}
# For all "valid" uvp6 Calanus images with segmentations

binsize <-  100
uvp6_allBin <- uvp6 %>%
  
  filter(type != "predicted")  %>% 
  mutate(depthBin = floor(depth/binsize)*binsize) %>% 
  mutate(depthRange = paste0(depthBin,"m - ",depthBin+binsize,"m")) %>% 
  mutate(depthBin = as.factor(depthBin)) %>% 
  select(depthRange, depthBin, prosome, lipid, lipidfullness, Major) %>% 
  group_by(depthRange, depthBin) %>%  
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), list(mean = mean,

            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  arrange(depthBin)
# Set range to factors
uvp6_allBin <- uvp6_allBin %>% 
  mutate(depthRange = factor(depthRange,
                                levels = unique(uvp6_allBin$depthRange)))

# add cummulative number and percent of images
uvp6_allBin <- uvp6_allBin %>% 
  mutate(percent = lipid_n / sum(lipid_n) * 100) %>% 
  mutate(cumtotal = cumsum(lipid_n),
         cumpercent = cumsum(percent)) %>% 
  mutate(cumpercentRev = 100 - cumpercent)


cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(uvp6_allBin, aes(y = depthRange, 
                          x = lipid_n)) +
    geom_point() +
    xlab("N images") + ylab("Depth bin") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev),
  
  ggplot(uvp6_allBin, aes(y = depthRange, 
                          x = cumpercent)) +
    geom_point() +
    xlab("% images") + ylab("Depth bin") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev),
  labels = "auto"
)


ggsave("figures/UVP6_overall_vertical_dist.png",
       height = 4, width = 6, units = "in")
```

# Plot proportion of images with segmentations relative to total living zoop images and total copepod images
```{r}
# The uvp6 data from ecotaxa
load("data/uvp6_deam_living_20250320.RData")

# Merge the 2021 an 2023 data 
uvp6_ecotaxa <- bind_rows(uvp6_de, uvp6_am) 
rm(uvp6_de, uvp6_am)

# Metadata of samples
meta_uvp6 <- uvp6_ecotaxa %>% 
  distinct(sample_id, lon = object_lon, lat = object_lat,
           botdep = sample_bottomdepth, date = object_date) %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>% 
  mutate(Year = year(date),
         Month = month(date),
         DOY = yday(date)) %>% 
  mutate(Year = as.factor(Year)) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id) %>% 
  filter(row_number() == 1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 8, "August", "")) %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 9, "September", Month2)) %>% 
  mutate(Month2 = if_else(Month == 10, "October", Month2)) %>% 
  select(-Month) %>% rename(Month = Month2) %>% 
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = c("August","September","October"))) 

# Get abundance
abund <- uvp6_ecotaxa %>%
  # separate copepods to with or without segmentations
  mutate(taxagroup = if_else(object_id %in% uvp6$object_id,
                              "Copepoda_segmented", taxagroup)) %>% 
  # identify specific copepods with no segmentation
  mutate(taxagroup = if_else(taxagroup == "Copepoda",
                             taxaname, taxagroup)) %>% 
  rename(lon = object_lon, lat = object_lat, 
         date = object_date, depth = object_depth_min,
         volume_m3 = Sampled_volume_m3) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, lon, lat, Depth_5m, volume_m3, taxagroup) %>% 
  summarise(nimgs = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(abundance = nimgs/volume_m3)

# # Check if all copepod with segmentation images are accounted for
# ii <- uvp6_ecotaxa %>% 
#   filter(object_id %in% uvp6_all$object_id)
# jj <- uvp6_all %>% 
#   filter(object_id %notin% uvp6_ecotaxa$object_id)


# To get abundance at other bin sizes, need to full join ?the volume data in uvp6_volumes so it records the bins with zero abundance. Easier if the ecopart data is pre binned
binsize <-  100
uvp6_ecopartBin <- uvp6_ecopart %>% 
  mutate(depthBin = floor(Depth_5m/binsize)*binsize) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, depthBin) %>% 
  summarise(volume_m3 = sum(Sampled_volume_m3),
            nbins = n(), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(binsize = binsize)

# integrated to 50 m depth bins [must sum individuals and divide by volume BUT including zero abundances], not just average

abundBin <- abund %>% 
  mutate(depthBin = floor(Depth_5m/binsize)*binsize) %>% 
  select(-c(Depth_5m, volume_m3, abundance)) %>% 
  left_join(uvp6_ecopartBin %>% select(-nbins),
            by = join_by(sample_id, depthBin)) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, lon, lat, depthBin, taxagroup, binsize, volume_m3) %>% 
  summarise(nimgsBin = sum(nimgs),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(abundanceBin = nimgsBin / volume_m3)
  
# Total abundance and copepod fraction
abundBinTotal <- abundBin %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, lon, lat, depthBin, binsize) %>% 
  summarise(abundanceTotal = sum(abundanceBin), 
            nimgsTotal = sum(nimgsBin),
            .groups = "drop")  %>% 
  # Copepod with segmentation fraction of abundance
  left_join(abundBin %>% 
              filter(taxagroup == "Copepoda_segmented") %>% 
              select(sample_id, depthBin, abundCope = abundanceBin),
            by = join_by(sample_id, depthBin)) %>% 
  mutate(copepod_frac = abundCope/abundanceTotal) %>% 
  mutate(copepod_frac = if_else(is.na(copepod_frac),
                                0, copepod_frac))


ggplot(abundBinTotal, aes(y = abundanceTotal, x = depthBin,
                          fill = copepod_frac)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = sample_id), alpha = 0.4)+
  geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  guides(color="none")


ggplot(abundBinTotal, aes(y = copepod_frac, x = depthBin)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  coord_flip() +
  ylab("Proporiton of images with segmentations") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  guides(color="none")
```

```{r}
  group_by(sample_id, depthBin) %>%
```
